s.note: Warm roasted peanuts with smoky chilli salt. John keeps snatching June's peanut.
s.how: Toss the peanuts with the oil and spread on a tray. Roast at 180C, shaking once, until golden. Toss hot with the paprika, cayenne, sugar and salt, then cool a little.

s.note: Buttermilk biscuits under peppery sausage gravy, ladled onto the tray.
s.how: Rub the butter into the flour with a pinch of salt, then stir in the buttermilk to a soft dough. Pat out 3cm thick, cut 8 rounds and bake at 220C until risen and golden. Brown the sausage mince, breaking it up, then stir in the plain flour. Whisk in the milk and simmer until thick, then season with plenty of pepper. Split the biscuits and ladle over the gravy.

m.note: Roast turkey with cornbread stuffing, gravy and cranberry sauce, on a steel tray.
m.how: Rub the turkey with half the butter, the sage and salt, and roast at 180C until the juices run clear. Soften the onion and celery in the rest of the butter, then mix with the cornbread, egg and 250ml stock. Bake the stuffing in a dish alongside the turkey for the last 35 minutes. Rest the turkey, stir the flour into the pan juices, whisk in the rest of the stock and simmer to a gravy. Slice and serve with the stuffing, gravy and cranberry sauce.

m.note: Ground beef and bean chili ladled onto the tray with a square of cornbread.
m.how: Brown the mince with the onion and garlic, then stir in the chilli powder, cumin and paprika. Add the tomatoes, beans and a cup of water and simmer until thick. For the cornbread, mix the polenta, flour, baking powder, sugar and salt, then stir in the milk, egg and melted butter. Pour into a buttered tin and bake at 200°C until golden. Ladle the chili into bowls with a square of cornbread.

w.n: Ring of Fire cinnamon bundt cake
w.note: Warm slices of brown sugar bundt cake in cinnamon glaze.
w.how: Beat the butter and brown sugar until pale, then beat in the eggs one at a time. Fold in the flour and half the cinnamon, alternating with the buttermilk. Spoon into a greased bundt tin and bake at 170C until a skewer comes out clean. Whisk the icing sugar, milk, the rest of the cinnamon and the cayenne, and pour over the cooled ring.

d.note: Fresh lemonade poured over ice, cold enough for a prison show.
d.how: Simmer the barley in the water with the lemon peel. Strain, stir in the sugar to dissolve and cool. Add the lemon juice and pour over ice.
